title: Sign-Along Singing
strapline: Songs with signs for the key words — so every child can join in, be understood, and reach communication through their hands.
intent: Children who don't yet talk get a bridge to communication — signing a key word gives them a way to join and be understood.
Children learn that signing is for everyone here, so no child is singled out for using their hands to communicate.
Children reinforce vocabulary through multiple channels at once — hearing the word, seeing the sign, doing the action.
Children build shared attention, turn-taking and the joy of doing something together in a group.
Children develop the fine and gross motor coordination that signing and action songs demand.
implementation: Choose a handful of favourite songs and sign the key words consistently — more, again, stop, milk, sleep, home — using a recognised sign vocabulary and keeping it simple.
Sign as a whole team, all day, not just at song time — the same sign at snack, at the door, at nappy time — so it becomes a real shared language.
Slow songs right down, pause on the key word, and give children the space to sign it back before you carry on.
Always pair the sign with the spoken word and the object where you can — sign 'milk', say 'milk', show the cup.
Follow babies' lead: even a rough approximation of a sign is a triumph — respond to it warmly and immediately.
Send the songs and signs home so families can join in and the vocabulary travels between nursery and house.
key_questions: Can you show me the sign for 'more'?
Shall we sing it again — do the sign to tell me!
Which song would you like — point or sign to choose?
Did you see how their hands said 'finished'?
What does this sign mean, do you think?

impact.text: Children use gesture, signs and first words to show wants and share attention.
Children join in favourite songs and rhymes with words, signs and actions and ask for them by name.
Children take turns in back-and-forth exchanges, vocalising or signing and waiting for a reply.
Children respond to familiar words in routines, supported by a consistent sign.
Children copy simple actions in songs and games — clap, wave, sign.

enhancements: A sign-of-the-week displayed with a photo, learned by the whole room including families at pick-up.
A song box of props and picture cards children pick from to request their favourite.
A slowed, quieter version for a baby room where signs are introduced one at a time.
A visiting older child or parent who signs, sharing songs across rooms and building community.
Recording the setting's signed songs so supply staff and new families learn the same signs.

playing_exploring: Children delight in the actions, signs and rhythms, exploring language with their whole body.
Babies and toddlers experiment with approximating signs, testing what gets a response.
active_learning: Being understood when they sign a want motivates children to sign again.
Children persist to master a tricky sign and beam when they get it, and are understood.
creating_thinking: Children connect a sign, a spoken word and a real object into one shared meaning.
They begin choosing signs to communicate beyond song time, using the tool flexibly.
